intro: A plain checklist for planning a first serious mountain trip. It is not a replacement for a course or a guide.

sections.title: Before you go
items: Get fit for the trip you are planning. Long days with a loaded pack are the best training.
Take a course in basic mountaineering skills: ropework, crampons, ice axe and self-arrest.
Start on easy peaks and build up. Do not jump to a big mountain on your first trip.
See a doctor, especially if you have a heart or lung condition, and get your vaccinations.
Buy travel insurance that covers rescue at the altitude you will be at.

sections.title: What to carry
items: Map, compass and a charged phone or GPS.
Head torch with spare batteries.
Sun protection: glacier glasses, sun cream and a hat.
First aid kit and a bivouac sack or emergency blanket.
Enough food and water, plus a spare day of food.
Extra layers, hat, gloves and a waterproof shell.

sections.title: On the mountain
items: Tell somebody your plan and when you expect to be back.
Check the forecast the night before and again in the morning.
Set a turnaround time and keep to it, whatever the weather looks like.
Eat and drink little and often.
Watch your partners, and speak up if someone looks unwell.

sections.title: Respect
items: Leave no trace. Carry your rubbish down, including human waste where it is required.
Respect local customs and sacred peaks.
Pay guides, porters and cooks fairly, and make sure they have proper kit and insurance.
Do not leave fixed ropes or gear behind.
Follow permit rules for the country you are in.
